title: Hardening multi-region SLOs with tenant-aware load-shedding and control-plane isolation
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem statement: Dedicated and Private customers require predictable tail-latency and availability during cross-region outages and control-plane upgrades. Current behavior: during region degradation we have seen noisy neighbor amplification where a handful of tenants exhaust node capacity (KV cache pressure + large batch requests), causing other tenants to miss SLOs. Control-plane operations in private deployments (k8s upgrades, operator restarts) can also create a transient window where tenant routing becomes inconsistent, sometimes causing double-routing and throttling storms.

Goal: Implement a coordinated solution that preserves per-tenant SLOs across multi-region failovers by combining:
  1) Strong SLO definitions and alerting (P50/P95/P99 token latency + availability) per deployment tier,
  2) Tenant-aware circuit breakers and prioritized load-shedding that operate both at the node and front-door routing layers,
  3) Control-plane isolation primitives for Dedicated/Private installs to ensure upgrades and control-plane failures do not cause cross-tenant blast radius,
  4) A deterministic multi-region failover policy with safe-rollback that can be exercised in chaos tests and runbooks.

Why this is important: Customers pay for reserved capacity and predictable latency; failure to isolate noisy tenants leads to outages and escalations. Private customers expect minimal operational disruption during control-plane maintenance. This ticket coordinates engineering work necessary to deliver an end-to-end, verifiable mitigation set.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Define SLO targets for Dedicated/Private tiers and add them to the SLO dashboard (P50/P95/P99 latency, success-rate) + alerting thresholds.
2) Implement per-tenant circuit breaker that trips on sustained CPU/KV cache pressure or token-per-second overage; circuit breakers expose reason codes and suggested backoff.
3) Implement prioritized load-shedding at the routing gateway: capacity-aware token budget that favors pinned/reserved tenants and degrades best-effort tenants first.
4) Control-plane can be upgraded in a staggered mode (per-region operator upgrade) with a pre-upgrade isolation phase that prevents routing flaps; exercise via canary upgrades and verify failover SLOs in staging.
5) Run a runbooked chaos exercise (simulated region loss + operator restart) and show SLO retention for >=95% of pinned tenants; document results and required rollbacks.
6) Add telemetry for tripped circuit breakers and shed events to the Console (per-tenant) and a new dashboard for on-call visibility.
plan:
Milestones:
1) SLO definition + dashboard (2 weeks): draft SLOs with PM and CS, add to internal dashboards, wire alerts. Assigned: Mateo.
2) Circuit breaker prototype (3 weeks): implement node-level breaker that monitors KV cache eviction rate, CPU, and per-tenant token rate; initially local to runtime with feature flag. Assigned: Priya Rao.
3) Routing-layer load-shedding (4 weeks): implement prioritized token budgets at gateway + backpressure headers; integrate with circuit-breaker signals. Assigned: Mateo + Networking.
4) Control-plane isolation primitives (3 weeks): ops API to quiesce routing config during upgrades, operator changes to perform staged upgrades, and an upgrade-checker that simulates failover. Assigned: Dan Kim.
5) End-to-end test & chaos exercise (2 weeks): staging run with multi-region failover simulated, collect metrics and adjust thresholds.
6) Documentation & runbook (1 week): release playbook, customer-facing notes for Private/Dedicated customers.

Technical notes: Use existing prefix/KV cache telemetry and extend per-tenant counters. Circuit breaker state must be persisted to avoid thundering-hero effect at restart. The routing gateway should expose per-request headers to indicate shed/circuit-breaker decisions for downstream observability. Feature-flag rollout via console-2026.03 for gradual enablement.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Overly aggressive shedding could violate SLAs for some customers. Mitigation: staged rollout, safety threshold that never sheds pinned/reserved tenants below a reserved baseline.
Risk: Circuit-breaker state loss on operator restart could cause mass re-open storms. Mitigation: persist state in the local node disk and reconcile from control-plane with exponential backoff.
Risk: Private deployments have heterogeneous networking and may not support the same backpressure semantics. Mitigation: provide a compatibility shim and a fallback to per-node local shedding that is conservative by default.
Risk: Increased telemetry and dashboards add cost. Mitigation: sample and prioritize metrics for on-call use; full retention only for post-incident analysis.
comments: 2026-02-25 - Ava Chen: Kickoff meeting notes: PM (Suresh) and Solutions Eng (Camille) emphasized customer expectations for reserved capacity during failovers. Decided to prioritize tenant-aware shedding over wholesale throttling.

2026-03-02 - Mateo Ruiz: Implemented initial SLO definitions in the SLO service; dashboards created under Console > Reliability > Dedicated. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4218

2026-03-04 - Priya Rao: Prototype circuit breaker merged behind feature flag; node-level breaker checks KV eviction rate and per-tenant token qps. Observed 12% drop in tail-latency in staging when breaker tripped for misbehaving tenant. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/789
2026-03-08 - Dan Kim: POC for control-plane quiesce API ready. Needs security review (RBAC) before enabling in Private installs. Open issue for RBAC review: SEC-1921

2026-03-11 - Ops (SLA on-call): Ran a simulated region-loss test in staging; discovered a router race where two regions attempted to re-route the same tenant leading to temporary duplicate sessions. Action: add leader-election token for routing decisions.
